source.title: protecting qwen3-8b from gcg based persona jailbreaks by steering with a linear direction

page_placements.theme: Analogues: contrastive single directions for other behaviours and concepts (not refusal)

record.file_problem: None; the full post is present.
record.tranche_reason: The post probes and steers assistant-persona behavior under GCG triggers, not refusal behavior or a refusal direction. It neither tests nor relies on the refusal claim.
record.gate_note: The reported probe and steering results concern persona classification and persona rates, not refusal of harmful or harmless user requests. They are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The post studies an 'assistant persona' direction in Qwen3-8b under entropy-optimised GCG triggers. It measures persona rates and persona-probe AUROC, never refusal of harmful or harmless user requests, and never a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. This is a related construct: a linear direction that mediates a jailbreak-induced behaviour, but the behaviour is persona adoption, not refusal. No claim version is tested, and the post does not mention refusal or the original paper.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct but incomplete. The author also claims that steering cuts non-assistant personas about 10x, and that random-direction controls show the directions are causally valid. The author also says GCG persona jailbreaks work by activating persona vectors, then hedges that the directions are partly token counters after debiasing.
record.recipe_differences: The post probes assistant-persona representations and steers persona outcomes under GCG triggers; it does not use the refusal-direction measurement or refusal interventions in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe results vary with token count and activation context. Steering outcomes differ between full-rollout and answer-only directions and between raw and z-space coordinates. The author reports that z-scoring materially changes answer-only steering.

fits_no_version.finding: Mass-mean probes on early answer tokens predict assistant vs non-assistant persona above a bag-of-tokens control (e.g. 0.81 vs 0.68 at 1 token). The gap shrinks with more tokens (0.93 vs 0.91 at 64), and INLP debiasing pulls AUROC to about or below the control.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona adoption under GCG triggers is linearly decodable in Qwen3-8b, but partly via lexical/token cues.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the full-rollout persona direction (+0.35) cuts the non-assistant persona rate from 33% to 3% (raw) or 5% (z-space). Subtracting it raises the rate to 43% (raw) or 75% (z-space). Random directions leave the rate at 32–33%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single linear persona direction causally shifts GCG-induced persona adoption in both directions, analogous to but distinct from refusal mediation.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully coherent rates change under steering: up to 77% with +0.35 raw full-rollout, and down to 22% with −0.35. Coherence is not a capability benchmark.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona steering trades off with output coherence in some directions.

record.problems: The author reports only one model and one prompt, 60 rollouts per steering condition, and no uncertainty estimates. Steering outcomes are judged by local Claude Code Sonnet 5 subagents. The coherence measure is not a general capability check. The author also reports that debiasing reduces probe accuracy below the bag-of-tokens control.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix's INLP probe table and debiased-steering table are not included. They report many additional debiasing variants and metrics, but these are persona-specific and do not test any claim version; the flattened steering results also do not clearly identify which direction source corresponds to each listed row.

untested.parts: No refusal direction is extracted, ablated or added; no refusal or capability measures.
GCG is studied, but persona adoption is the outcome, not suppression of a refusal direction; no adversarial training against ablation.
One model; no transfer of a refusal direction.
No refusal in reasoning models; Qwen3-8b reasoning is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Persona rate here means the rate of non-assistant personas. The rows are accurately transcribed and correctly unlinked from all versions. The appendix INLP steering tables lack clear direction-source labels, so leaving them out is reasonable. Single model, single prompt, 60 rollouts, LLM judge, no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No refusal direction is measured or ablated; no harmful-request compliance, harmless-request refusal, or general capability evaluation.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
GCG triggers are used to induce persona changes, but the post does not test suppression of a refusal direction or robustness training against its ablation.
No claim about the geometry or number of refusal directions is tested.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal decision is measured.
Only Qwen3-8b is studied; transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages is not tested.
No refusal training method, timing, or resulting refusal direction is studied.
No reasoning-model refusal behavior is studied.
